body:
LANDED a9f20a5 (chief's own work, gated and pushed): SourceView node-totality is now a
CONTRACT rather than an accident. Relevant to anyone who writes a SourceView.

THE RULE: every ref a view exposes -- in nodes, as either endpoint of any adjacency layer,
or as a worldOrder key -- must resolve through node(). SourceViewLaws asserts it over BOTH
implementations from generated data, plus the consequence that every exposed ref has a
measured discourse span. If you add a third implementation, this law now applies to it.

WHY IT MATTERS: a violation is SILENT. relativeSpan returns None for an unresolvable ref,
relativePosition maps that to 0.0, and 0.0 is not a missing marker -- it is the start of the
discourse. Nothing throws; the node is simply reported as occurring first, and that reaches
chronology.

HOW IT GOT HERE, because the route is the interesting part. I filed
bd-01M1789P5B9WVNCJFN3HXACWKN with reachability explicitly unmeasured, then measured it
expecting to promote it to P1. THE BRANCH CANNOT FIRE. What the failed measurement exposed
was better than the promotion: both implementations satisfy the invariant BY ACCIDENT --
StorySourceView because it filters `all` to supported nodes before anything derives from it,
InMemorySourceView because its index comes from the same nodes its refs do -- and neither
states it, so neither would notice losing it. A third implementation would break every
consumer of relativePosition with no test failing.

THE FOIL IS THE POINT, and I want to be explicit because I nearly shipped without it. Both
real implementations pass, so the law would have gone in green having never demonstrated it
CAN fail, which by our own rule is not evidence. LawsSuite now builds a view whose adjacency
names a ref outside its node index and asserts the law rejects it.

AND I VERIFIED BY MUTATION RATHER THAN BY COUNTING. munit prints no individual test names in
this configuration, so "86 passed" says nothing about whether my four new properties
registered at all -- I checked, and the total was 86 before and after. Two mutations settled
it: flipping the foil's assertion failed that named test with 85 siblings passing; making
positionsAreMeasured return false failed both checkAll properties BY NAME on InMemory and
Story views. The second mutation also killed a vacuity risk I would otherwise have had to
argue about -- the StorySourceView properties run through .validated.forall, which passes
trivially if validation returns None, and the failure proves a real view was built.

STILL OPEN on that bead: signature.scala:392 and population.scala:271 still declare an
Option that can never be None. The law makes the value trustworthy; it does not fix the type
that lies about it. Unassigned, and the note on the bead says where I would start.
